pillars.rationale: Updated DRM law in 2019; clear roles for ministry and decentralized units but limited enforcement capacity.
National hazard mapping exists but is incomplete and not regularly updated.
Coastal and urban risk-reduction projects exist but lack national standards.
Functional national emergency operations center; subnational preparedness uneven.
No dedicated sovereign financial protection instrument or contingency lines.
Reconstruction guidelines drafted but not yet adopted into procurement rules.

indicators.indicator_name: National DRM/DRR law with defined institutional mandates
indicators.explanation: A comprehensive DRM law was passed in 2019 (Presidential Decree No. 26/19) establishing clear mandates for national and municipal disaster management authorities. The law defines roles for the National Civil Protection and Fire Service (SNPCB) and coordinates with sectoral ministries.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: Presidential Decree No. 26/19 establishes mandates for DRM coordination across government levels.

indicators.indicator_name: National DRM/DRR strategy or policy document in place
indicators.explanation: The National Disaster Risk Reduction Strategy (2020-2030) was adopted and includes targets aligned with the Sendai Framework. Implementation has begun in pilot provinces but nationwide rollout is incomplete.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: National Strategy 2020-2030 aligns with Sendai Framework priorities and includes M&E indicators.

indicators.indicator_name: Systems for recording historical disaster impacts and hazard mapping
indicators.explanation: Angola developed flood hazard maps for major river basins in 2018 through a World Bank project. However, maps do not yet cover drought, coastal erosion, or all provinces. A national disaster loss database was initiated but lacks consistent data entry protocols.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: Flood hazard mapping completed for Cunene and Kwanza basins covering approximately 40% of territory.

indicators.indicator_name: Public accessibility of risk information and data platforms
indicators.explanation: Risk data is maintained by SNPCB but is not publicly accessible. No open data platform exists; stakeholders must request information through official channels with variable response times.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: Risk information managed internally; formal requests required for external access.

indicators.indicator_name: Integration of DRM into land-use planning and urban development
indicators.explanation: Urban master plans for Luanda and Benguela include flood risk zones and building restrictions in high-risk areas. However, enforcement is weak and informal settlements continue to expand in restricted zones.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: Luanda Master Plan 2019 designates flood-prone areas; enforcement mechanisms under development.

indicators.indicator_name: Disaster/climate risk integration in National Public Investment System
indicators.explanation: The Public Investment Manual was updated in 2021 to include risk screening guidelines for infrastructure projects exceeding $10 million. Application is inconsistent across ministries and lacks dedicated technical capacity for risk assessment.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: Public Investment Manual 2021 requires risk screening for projects over $10M threshold.

indicators.indicator_name: Early warning systems for forecasting and dissemination
indicators.explanation: The National Institute of Meteorology (INAMET) operates weather stations and issues flood forecasts during rainy season. SMS-based early warning reaches approximately 60% of at-risk communities. Integration with community-level response protocols is improving.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: INAMET early warning system operational with 60% coverage of at-risk populations via SMS alerts.

indicators.indicator_name: Emergency preparedness and response plans with multi-level coordination
indicators.explanation: National contingency plans exist and are activated annually during flood season. Provincial civil protection commissions coordinate with national level. Regular simulation exercises conducted in 8 of 18 provinces.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: National contingency plan activated annually; provincial coordination through civil protection commissions.

indicators.indicator_name: Assessment of contingent liabilities and fiscal exposure to disasters
indicators.explanation: No comprehensive fiscal risk assessment for disasters has been conducted. The Ministry of Finance does not systematically track disaster-related expenditures or model potential fiscal impacts of major disaster scenarios.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: Disaster fiscal risk assessment not conducted; contingent liabilities not quantified systematically.

indicators.indicator_name: Disaster Risk Financing strategy backed by legal framework
indicators.explanation: Angola does not have a formal DRF strategy. Emergency response is funded through ad-hoc budget reallocations. Discussions are underway with development partners to develop a layered financing approach.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: No DRF strategy in place; emergency funding via ad-hoc reallocations from national budget.

indicators.explanation: Reconstruction guidelines were drafted in 2022 following major floods. Guidelines include 'build back better' principles but have not been formally adopted into government procurement rules or budgeting processes.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: Draft reconstruction guidelines (2022) include resilience principles; adoption into procurement pending.

indicators.indicator_name: Post-Disaster Needs Assessment tools and methodology
indicators.explanation: Angola participated in PDNA training in 2020 and conducted a pilot assessment after 2021 floods in Cunene Province. The PDNA methodology is recognized but not yet institutionalized as standard practice for all disasters.
indicators.evidence_excerpt: PDNA pilot completed for 2021 Cunene floods; methodology recognized but not institutionalized.
